title: Epochal credit resolver and spike-protection reconciler for late-arriving tokens
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build an epoch-oriented credit resolver job that absorbs bursty/late token events, produces deterministic per-tenant credit adjustments, and avoids double-counting during region-failover and multi-route fanout. This work sits in the console backend usage analytics pipeline and replaces brittle heuristics currently causing invoice noise during spikes and backfills.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end run for a 24-hour test window yields deterministic tenant credits that reconcile to source logs within 0.1% for non-overlap cases
Late-arrival events ingested up to 72 hours are reconciled and produce idempotent downstream adjustments (no duplicate credits on replays)
Job exposes per-epoch diagnostics: reconciled_count, late_count, dup_suppressed_count, uncertainty_score
No increase in median job runtime beyond 15% of current baseline; memory footprint remains within existing worker limits
Integration tests covering multi-region replay and simulated broker reordering with golden snapshots are added to CI
implementation_notes: Introduce an epoch marker (tenant_id, epoch_start_iso) and persist a compact epoch manifest to S3 for deterministic retries
Switch from naive dedupe to an idempotent fencing key: sha256(tenant + request_id + model_route + timestamp_bucket)
Use RocksDB local index for per-worker seen-set with TTL based on configured max-late-window (default 72h) to keep memory bounded
When spikes exceed worker capacity, fall back to approximate spillover counting using count-min sketch; mark epoch uncertainty_score > 0 and surface to billing UX
Make the job transactional with two-phase commit to ledger: stage adjustments to a staging table, run validation passes, then atomically apply via existing accounting API
Retain lightweight provenance pointers (source_event_id) for any applied adjustments to enable human troubleshooting and automated rollback
data_schema_changes: Add epochs table: (tenant_id TEXT, epoch_iso TEXT, state ENUM, reconciled_at TIMESTAMP, provenance_snapshot_s3 TEXT)
Add adjustments staging table: (adjustment_id UUID, tenant_id, amount_tokens INT, reason TEXT, source_event_ids ARRAY<TEXT>, applied BOOLEAN)
Extend existing token_events schema with request_bucket_iso and model_route_id to make attribution deterministic
rollout_plan: 1) Run job in shadow mode for 48h against production traffic and compare outputs with current production reconciler (diff stats stored in /dashboards/epochal-resolver-shadow)
2) Enable controlled apply for 1% of tenants (random sample with holdback), monitor invoice deltas and manual review queue
3) Ramp to 25% and then 100% once stability and accuracy KPIs met
4) After 100% rollout, retire old heuristic reconciler and keep shadow for 7 days to validate post-cutover
testing_plan: Unit tests for fencing key calculation, RocksDB TTL eviction, and count-min sketch fallback
Integration test harness that replays historical s3 event batches with induced delays and reordering
Golden snapshot tests: deterministic run against a curated 7-day production trace should match expected ledger adjustments
Load test: simulate multi-tenant spike (100x baseline events) and verify spillover behaviour and retention of cleanup invariants
monitoring_and_alerting: Create dashboard: epochal_resolver.overview (reconciled_count, late_count, dup_suppressed_count, avg_latency)
Alert on sustained uncertainty_score > 0.1 for top-10 tenants for 10min
Audit log export for any applied adjustments older than 48h for manual finance review
